reason: The arterial wall is unlined, and the lining cells form a blood-facing surface, so they look like a natural match.
expectation: The cells will line the elastic wall to make an artery.

alternatives.reason: The picture also clearly suggests bringing these together for exchange.

effect: The lining and elastic wall made arteries that carry blood away from the heart, completing that goal.
reaction: The result matched the picture I expected.
reason: The body cells are pictured beside capillary outlines, matching the exchange-vessel goal.
expectation: The capillaries will be placed close to the cells so materials can be exchanged.

effect: The capillary bed brings blood close to cells, allowing oxygen and nutrients out and carbon dioxide in.
reaction: The exchange is clearer from seeing the arrows in both directions.
reason: The venous wall needs a lining, just as the arterial wall did.
expectation: The lining cells will make a smooth inner surface for the vein.

alternatives.reason: The valve flaps also belong in the return route, though the wall is still unlined.

effect: The lined veins provide the return route toward the heart, but they still need valves.
reaction: The result matched the arterial lining step.
reason: The valve flaps are pictured inside a vein and match the remaining goal.
expectation: The veins will gain valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

effect: The veins now have valves, and the remaining goal is to join the three vessel routes.
reaction: The picture makes it clearer how a contracting muscle can help move blood forward.
reason: Blood travels outward through arteries and then reaches capillaries, so these routes should connect.
expectation: The arteries and capillary bed will join, leaving the venous return to connect afterward.

effect: The artery now branches into the capillary bed, with open ends for the return route.
reason: The open collecting ends should connect to the venous return to join all three routes.
expectation: The veins will connect the capillary bed to the return route toward the heart.

effect: The veins completed the route from arteries through capillaries and back toward the heart, finishing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate routes form one continuous network.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the capillary bed was most worthwhile: the arrows showed oxygen and nutrients moving to cells and carbon dioxide moving toward the blood.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the veins felt a little repetitive after lining the arteries, although it made sense.

surprise.text: The valve picture showed how a contracting muscle can help push blood forward while the valves prevent backward flow.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the pairings understandable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because connecting the parts into a complete route was satisfying and the exchange picture helped explain what the vessels do.
